hero.headline: Nasdaq fell 5.3% as Nvidia lost 14%. Here is how the AI rout reaches your 401(k).
hero.dek: Every story on FIOPO is traced to where it lands: your fuel, your rent, your savings, your job. Here is how today's biggest story travels.

chain.label: The event
chain.text: Nvidia fell 14.01% to $125.53 on Friday after Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, said SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues. About $491 billion in value was erased.

chain.label: The index
chain.text: The Nasdaq fell 5.28% to 22,617.73 and is now down for 2026. The S&P 500 lost 3.70% to 6,910.39, its seventh straight loss, and closed in correction.

chain.label: The chips
chain.text: AMD fell 13.25%, Micron 13.89% and Broadcom 12.19%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 10.73% in a day and 17.13% in a week.

chain.label: Fear gauge
chain.text: The VIX jumped 26.20% to 35.89, its highest close since late March. Only consumer staples rose, up 0.67%. Bitcoin fell below $60,000.

chain.label: You
chain.text: The S&P 500 lost 8.6% this week, its worst week since April 2025. Nvidia is one of the biggest holdings in index funds, so most 401(k) savers felt this directly.

hero.caption: Sources: Longbridge, CappNotes and The Motley Fool, November 20, 2026. The chain itself is FIOPO analysis.

stories.headline: Gas fell to $3.69, its lowest since March, as markets price in a December rate hike.
stories.happened: The AAA national average was $3.69 on November 20, down from $3.90 on November 12 and $4.27 on October 22. Only eight states are above $4. North Carolina is cheapest at $3.04 and Hawaii highest at $5.59.
stories.happening: AAA says the average could fall another 15 cents by Thanksgiving, which would avoid a holiday record ($3.58 in 2022). At the same time CME FedWatch puts a 99.3% chance on a quarter point Fed hike at the December 8 to 9 meeting. Those are market odds, not a decision.

could.text: Cheaper gas helps this week's budget, but a rate hike would push card and loan rates higher within weeks.

you: Driving for Thanksgiving? Compare stations with a price app before you fill up.
Carrying a card balance? Pay down what you can before a December hike lifts variable rates.
Need a car loan or a fixed rate CD? Rates set before December 9 may be the better deal.

stories.headline: Iran sets seven conditions to reopen Hormuz. Oil still posts a third weekly loss.
stories.happened: Foreign Minister Araghchi said on Friday that seven conditions must be met before Hormuz reopens, including an end to the war and the lifting of sanctions and the US naval blockade. He ruled out sending Iran's 60% enriched uranium abroad. The US Treasury sanctioned four Iranians it called oil trustees.
stories.happening: Brent settled at $92.57 on Friday, up 0.64% on a reported tanker fire near Hormuz but down 3.41% for the week, its third weekly loss. WTI settled at $83.98, down 5.17% for the week. On Saturday Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the strait, a claim not independently confirmed.

could.note: FIOPO read for the next 30 days, unchanged from November 17. Iran's conditions make a quick deal less likely. Judgment, not fact.

you: Pump prices are still falling, so there is no need to stock up on fuel.
Holding energy funds? Oil has dropped about a fifth in November. Check that one sector is not a large share of your savings.
Flying through Gulf hubs? Keep bookings flexible while drones and blockade talks continue.

stories.headline: Nvidia's 14% fall follows an SEC report, a CEO exit and a state subpoena.
stories.happened: Reuters reported Friday that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia, after The Wall Street Journal said Tuesday that the SEC was investigating. The SEC declined to comment. Reuters noted that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing. On Thursday California's attorney general served Nvidia an investigative subpoena over whether China obtained advanced chips.
stories.happening: Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO earlier this month and Colette Kress is interim CEO. Nvidia reported revenue up 103% to $115.8 billion last quarter and expects about $130 billion this quarter. The stock is down about 48% from its record close of $239.24 on October 6.

could.text: Strong sales have not stopped the slide. Until the SEC review and the CEO search are clearer, expect big swings in Nvidia and in the funds that hold it.
could.note: FIOPO read. Judgment, not fact. Not investment advice.

you: Check how much of your savings sits in Nvidia through tech and S&P 500 funds. Many hold it as a top position.
Do not sell in a panic. Rebalance only if tech has grown past the share you planned.
Own single chip stocks? Decide your limit now and use limit orders, not market orders.
stories.watch: any statement from Nvidia or the SEC, and a permanent CEO pick.

sources.name: The Motley Fool, after the close

stories.headline: Gold and Bitcoin fell with stocks. Treasury bonds were the shelter.
stories.happened: Spot gold fell 1.88% to $3,557.96 on Friday and touched $3,513.54, its lowest since September 2025. It lost about 8% this week. Bitcoin fell 6.01% to $58,186 by early evening, below $60,000 for the first time since July. Ether fell 9.03%.
stories.happening: Investors moved into Treasuries. The 10 year yield fell 12 basis points to 4.92% and the 2 year to 4.63%. The dollar index is near a 19 month high, about 103.8.

could.text: With a rate hike priced in and the dollar strong, gold and crypto may stay under pressure. Falling yields help bond funds.

you: Bond funds gained as yields fell. A mix of stocks and bonds is doing its job this week.
Holding Bitcoin? Size it as money you could see fall by half.
Buying gold as insurance? It can fall alongside stocks, as it did this week.
stories.watch: whether Bitcoin holds near its 2026 low.

regions.covers: China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia
regions.headline: Foreign money into China's high tech industries rose 31%.
regions.text: China's commerce ministry said foreign investment in high tech industries reached 252.8 billion yuan ($38 billion) in January to October, up 31% from a year earlier. Total foreign investment fell 2.4% to 606.9 billion yuan.
regions.you: Foreign companies are still building China tech supply chains. Expect more Chinese made electronics and parts in what you buy.

regions.covers: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal
regions.headline: Indian stocks hit nine month highs while Wall Street fell.
regions.text: The Sensex rose 1.08% to 83,919.71 and the Nifty 1.12% to 25,800.60 on Friday, a fourth straight weekly gain. Foreign investors have put a record $12.21 billion into Indian stocks in November.
regions.you: Own an international fund? Check how much India it holds. Markets outside US tech are moving differently this month.

regions.covers: European Union, United Kingdom, Ukraine, Russia
regions.headline: Russian missiles land in Poland during an attack on Ukraine.
regions.text: Poland's defence minister said a Kh-101 cruise missile fell near Nowy Lipowiec, about 60 km from the Ukrainian border, a second missile at Rudnik nad Sanem and a likely drone at Mołodycz. No one was hurt. NATO said it stands in solidarity with Poland. The STOXX 600 fell 2.00%.
regions.you: Traveling in eastern Poland? Check government alerts. Defence spending in Europe is likely to keep rising.

regions.covers: Gulf states, Iran, Israel, Iraq, Yemen
regions.headline: Iran claims it shot down a US drone over Hormuz.
regions.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday a new air defence system downed a US MQ-9 over the Strait of Hormuz, which they called the 58th such drone. The claim was carried by Iranian state media and is not independently confirmed.
regions.you: Any clash near Hormuz can move oil quickly. Watch fuel prices before you lock in holiday travel.

regions.covers: Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Egypt
regions.headline: South Africa holds rates at 7.25% in a split vote.
regions.text: The South African Reserve Bank held its repo rate at 7.25% on Thursday by a 4 to 3 vote, with three members wanting a quarter point hike. October inflation rose to 5.2% from 4.5%. The next decision is January 28, 2027.
regions.you: Borrowing in rand? A close vote means a hike in January is a real possibility.

regions.headline: Argentina's peso hits 1,580 per dollar, its weakest in a year.
regions.text: The peso closed at 1,580 per dollar on Friday, its weakest close in at least 12 months. In Brazil the real closed near 5.93 on Thursday, its weakest close since January 2025, even after a reported $1 billion central bank dollar sale.
regions.you: A trip to Argentina or Brazil is getting cheaper in dollars. Families there pay more for imports.

sports.headline: Netflix, Amazon and Fox chase 2030 World Cup rights as ESPN and Apple sit out.
sports.text: Fox, bidding with TelevisaUnivision, plus Netflix and Amazon remain in the race for US rights to the 2030 men's World Cup. ESPN, Apple, Paramount Skydance and Telemundo are out, and YouTube did not bid. Fox and Telemundo paid $1.285 billion for 2026.
sports.you: Your 2030 World Cup may need a streaming subscription. Watch which service wins before you budget for it.

sources.name: Front Office Sports via Yahoo Sports

sports.headline: Vivid Seats hands lenders 80% of its stock in a $232 million debt deal.
sports.text: Front Office Sports reports the ticket resale company reached a $232 million debt deal that gives its lenders 80% of the company's stock.
sports.you: Buying resale tickets? Pay by credit card for chargeback protection, whatever platform you use.

sports.headline: New York's attorney general moves to block Kalshi sports contracts.
sports.text: Letitia James refiled a request in Manhattan Supreme Court for an order barring Kalshi's sports, culture and election contracts, with a proposed penalty of $100,000 per unauthorized contract. New York online sports betting handle fell 4% to $663.9 million in the week to November 15.
sports.you: Using prediction apps for sports? Rules are shifting by state. Keep balances small until courts decide.

entertainment.headline: The Hunger Games prequel is tracking for a $100 million plus opening.
entertainment.text: Boxoffice Pro forecasts Sunrise on the Reaping at $100 million to $120 million this weekend, November 20 to 22. That would be the first $100 million opener since Spider-Man: Brand New Day in July.
entertainment.you: Big openings sell out premium screens. Book ahead or wait a week for cheaper weekday seats.

entertainment.headline: Ramayana sets a UK record for an Indian film.
entertainment.text: Ramayana topped the UK and Ireland chart for November 6 to 8 with £1.7 million from 364 cinemas, a record for an Indian film. Indian cinemas have grossed ₹13,775 crore in 2026 through November 15, already a record year.
entertainment.you: Indian releases now open wide abroad. Check local listings early, since big titles sell out on opening weekend.

items.text: GTA 6 early access streams dominate. Kai Cenat's first play stream drew 6.2 million views in 22 hours.
Movie trailers crowd the list: Universal's The Comeback King has 6.2 million views and NEON's Artificial 4.5 million in two days.

innovation.headline: Pacific Fusion gets a first of its kind license in New Mexico.
innovation.text: Pacific Fusion received New Mexico's first radioactive materials license for a private fusion company, covering tritium at its $1 billion Albuquerque campus. It aims for net facility gain by 2030. In Japan, Helical Fusion won up to ¥19.2 billion ($126 million) in government support.
innovation.you: Fusion is still years from your power bill, but licenses like this are real steps. Be wary of anyone selling fusion stocks as a sure thing.

innovation.headline: A rechargeable battery that uses vitamin B12.
innovation.text: University of Cordoba researchers built a zinc air battery that uses vitamin B12 as its catalyst instead of costly metals. The prototype lasted up to 250 charge cycles.
innovation.you: Cheaper, safer battery materials could lower costs for home storage over time. This is still lab work.

innovation.headline: Anthropic's stock nears its IPO price on day two.
innovation.text: Anthropic fell 8.50% to $88.91 in its first full trading session on Friday. It touched $83.05, close to its $83 IPO price, as AI stocks sold off.
innovation.you: New listings swing hard. If you buy, set a price limit and size the position small.

travel.headline: Lake Balaton, Hungary: a lake holiday without Como's crowds.
travel.text: Lonely Planet named Lake Balaton one of its most underrated places for 2027, for summer festivals, castles and lavender fields, as an alternative to Lake Como.
travel.you: Planning summer 2027? Look at lakeside towns now, and pay in forint rather than accepting a card conversion to dollars.

travel.headline: St. Augustine, Florida: Spanish streets without a transatlantic flight.
travel.text: Lonely Planet's 2027 underrated list includes St. Augustine for centuries of history and Spanish style streets that give a European feel on a domestic trip.
travel.you: Want old Europe on a short break? A domestic trip skips passports and long haul fares. Check the official visitor site for events before you book.

travel.headline: The dollar buys more in Argentina and Brazil than in a year.
travel.text: Argentina's peso closed at 1,580 per dollar on November 20, its weakest in at least 12 months, and Brazil's real closed near 5.93, its weakest since January 2025. Lonely Planet's 2027 list also picks Bolivia and Quito.
travel.you: Pay in the local currency when a card terminal offers dollars, and use a card with no foreign transaction fee.

picks.title: What Should My Children Do?
picks.text: An economist asks what the next generation should learn, and what it should stop worrying about, in a world changed by AI. Useful for any family planning school or career choices.

picks.title: Primetime Preacher$
picks.text: A 113 minute film on Jim Bakker, Jerry Falwell and Jimmy Swaggart, three 1980s televangelists who built TV ministries before scandal. A sharp look at how money flows when trust is the product.

items.text: SpaceX caught a returning Starship upper stage with its launch tower arms for the first time, after 14 orbits. The booster was lost over the Gulf.
India won its first ODI cricket series in New Zealand in seven years, 3 to 1.
India beat Pakistan by one wicket to win the Under-19 Asia Cup, its ninth title.
NASA's Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth.
BepiColombo is entering orbit around Mercury, only the second spacecraft ever to do so.
ESA's Hera is arriving at the asteroid Didymos to study the crater from NASA's DART impact.
Artemis II splashed down off San Diego after a 10 day trip around the Moon, the first crewed lunar voyage in more than 50 years.
NASA's Perseverance set the record for distance driven on another world, more than 45 km on Mars.
The Hubble Space Telescope completed its 200,000th orbit of Earth.
